Expectation1: Look out for each other's safety and well-being
Situation1: One sibling is preparing to try a new skateboard trick on a steep, uneven ramp.
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Story: It was almost midnight when I heard the crash from the garage. My little brother, always chasing thrills, was about to try a new skateboard trick on the old, cracked ramp Dad warned us about. I knew I should be there, watching out for him, making sure he didn’t get hurt. But just as I reached for the door, my phone buzzed. It was Mia, my best friend. Her voice trembled through the speaker, thick with tears. She’d just gotten terrible news about her family, and she needed me to listen, to be there for her, even if only over the phone. My heart twisted. I could hear my brother’s board clatter again, louder this time, and I pictured him at the top of the ramp, ready to drop in. I wanted to run to him, to keep him safe. But Mia’s sobs pulled at me, too—she’d always been there for me, and now she needed me more than ever. I stood frozen in the hallway, torn between the two people who needed me most, feeling the weight of both their expectations pressing in on me.
